messages:
incbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High ephemeral-storage usage detected on k8s-nodes-usw-*/pools/runtime (3 nodes) — eviction risk for pods using /var/lib/modelcache. Autoscaled: false. triggered_at=1901827365

sara: getting paged, joining. seeing spikes in node ephemeral usage to >92% on three nodes. modelcache dirs are huge.

junaid: I'm on it — checking `kubectl top nodes` and `kubectl describe node` now.

cass: customer impact? any 5xx from API gateways?

oncall-runtime: yes, we have elevated 503s from hosted-api-prod -> routing to Dedicated fallback for some tenants. Not universal but high traffic customers on west region seeing timeouts.

matt: logs from runtime pods show repeated `OOM when allocating tensor` and `CUDA error: out of memory` interleaved with `kubelet eviction: Pod ... deleted` lines. snippet: ```
2026-03-15T14:02:10Z runtime: ERROR: CUDA OOM when allocating 1.4GiB
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z kubelet: eviction manager: attempting to reclaim ephemeral-storage
2026-03-15T14:02:13Z kubelet: eviction manager: evicting pod runtime-abcde due to imagefs.available<500MB
```

oncall-runtime: that's consistent with model cache growing until disk pressure forces kubelet to evict. Evicted pods lose GPU state -> subsequent cold start triggers OOMs due to KV cache restores.

junaid: reproduction: `du -sh /var/lib/modelcache/*` on node-7 shows `~420GB` for a single model shard; we currently have no upper bound on local cache per pod.

cass: ok immediate mitigations: 1) stop new deploys in west, 2) temporarily increase eviction pressure by freeing space, 3) migrate some traffic out of west, 4) triage on-call to run cleanup.

sara: I'll add the incident channel to the customer-facing incident page and set status: partial degradation for west-hosted-api. Notifying support.

oncall-runtime: executing cleanup plan: (A) scale down non-critical runtime replicas on affected nodes, (B) remove stale cache files older than 24h, (C) cordon+drain one worst node to force pods to reschedule to nodes with space.

matt: commands I'm going to run, sharing for visibility: ```
# list pods using model cache PVCs/local dirs
kubectl get pods -o wide --all-namespaces | grep runtime
# delete large stale cache files on node (run via ssh or debug pod)
sudo find /var/lib/modelcache -type f -mtime +1 -delete
# cordon + drain node
kubectl cordon k8s-nodelc-usw-7
kubectl drain k8s-nodelc-usw-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

tanvi: quick caution: `--delete-local-data` will evict pods that rely on local caches; they will cold-start and might spike memory/GPU usage on target nodes. We should throttle drain and move a few at a time.

oncall-runtime: acknowledged. we'll drain one node at a time and watch GPU mem and OOM rate. moving only low-QPS shards first.

ops-bot: :information_source: automated-scaling: reduced runtime noncritical replicas in west by 40% at 1901827438.

junaid: manual cleanup completed on node-7: removed ~260GB of stale modelcache (failed downloads, temp files). ephemeral available increased from 8% to 54%.

matt: after cleanup I'm seeing fewer eviction events but two pods still crash with CUDA OOM during startup: `runtime-init` logs show a race where multiple large models are being reloaded simultaneously. We need a short-term admission-control throttle.

cass: can we gate model load concurrency per node? maybe set an env var to limit parallel model loads for runtime worker.

oncall-runtime: yes we have `MODEL_LOAD_CONCURRENCY` in runtime config. I'm patching a configmap to set it to 1 for west pool. Applying now: `kubectl patch cm runtime-config -n infra --patch '{"data":{"MODEL_LOAD_CONCURRENCY":"1"}}'`

matt: after reducing concurrency, OOM rate dropped by ~80% during the next 10 minutes. Good.

sara: customer update: posting to status.redwood.ai — "Partial degradation in US-WEST: text-generation API experiencing elevated errors and latency for some customers. Routing-based fallbacks engaged. Engineers are mitigating. No data loss reported." — publishing now. :loudspeaker:

oncall-runtime: next steps: 1) keep `MODEL_LOAD_CONCURRENCY=1` until node-level caches stabilise, 2) schedule rolling restart of affected runtime pods to ensure new config picks up, 3) request infra to add ephemeral-storage eviction metrics and alerts for per-node /var/lib/modelcache usage, 4) follow-up postmortem.

tanvi: I'm taking the primary on-call handoff in 15m. I'll be the incident commander after that. handoff ETA: 1901828350.

matt: creating a short-term rule to avoid heavy cache writes during peak hours: patching modelcache prefetcher to back off if node ephemeral < 30%.

junaid: also adding a quick check to the scheduler: prefer nodes with >40% free ephemeral for large model shard scheduling. low-effort improvement via topologyHint.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: packed action items updated in incident tracker: cleanup done, concurrency throttle applied, node drained k8s-nodelc-usw-7, customer status posted.

cass: impact summary for stakeholders: affected ~14% of production traffic in US-WEST for ~45 minutes (14:02 -> 14:47). Major customers automatically fell back to Dedicated where configured; 3 customers saw 30-60s retries before fallback. No persisted data loss.

sara: support and AMs notified. collecting impacted tenant list now.

tanvi: taking over as IC (oncall-runtime -> tanvi). I'll coordinate post-handoff. I've pulled the logs and will watch OOMs and eviction events.

oncall-runtime: handoff complete. follow-up tasks assigned: permanent modelcache quota per pod, eviction-aware scheduler changes, improved observability for imagefs/ephemeral metrics.

matt: will open PRs for modelcache quota + prefetch backoff and link to incident ticket.

sara: thanks everyone. closing alert once metrics are stable for 30m. current status: degraded -> stabilizing. :thumbsup:"
